what: Makes the boundary between two sections eat in along cell-foam edges (WebGL). The previous section’s background color hangs jaggedly down to one screen depth over the top of the next section. While the boundary line travels from the bottom to the top of the screen (progress 0→1, following by .08 per frame), the remaining hang of 1.65·(1−s)² screens is eaten upward (for out, the next section’s color fills into the previous one by 1.65·s² screens). The edge is built from two layers of cells, grain, a center mound and small peaks, with bubble holes sparsely punched toward the front, and it boils in 24 steps per second. When scrolled fast, the middle swells by the scroll speed (.2×, max .3 screen) and then settles back

options.direction: in (default, the previous section’s color stretches then gets swallowed) or out (the next section’s color fills up over the previous one)
options.look: jagged (default, finely uneven) or dissolve (large cells with big bumps, as in the recording)
options.travel: Distance it is eaten upward (screens), default 1.65
options.overlap: Depth of overlap onto the opposite side (screen), default .35
options.catch: Rate of following progress (per frame), default .08
